prompt: A hiking trail is marked like a number line. One trail marker sits at $-4$ and another sits at $6$. How many units apart are they?
hint: Distance is never negative — it is just how far you walk.

hints.text: Distance is never negative — it is just how far you walk.
On a number line, distance is $|$larger $-$ smaller$|$: $|6 - (-4)|$.

explanation: The distance between two points on a number line is the absolute value of their difference.
Walking from $-4$ up to $0$ is 4 units, then $0$ up to $6$ is 6 more: $4 + 6 = 10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count through zero
steps: From $0$ to $6$ you cover 6 more. Total: $4 + 6 = 10$ units.
